headline: Apple has said it will add stricter controls to the Mac setting that lets an app read everything on a computer, citing the rise of AI agents.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered by 2: Apple announced this on 2 Oct and our 3 Oct edition carried it; Mashable adds no new date or control details.
importance_line: What changed is a repeat of Apple's plan to make users approve Full Disk Access explicitly, which affects Mac users first, then makers of AI agents and other apps, and the doubt is that no start date or design of the new controls has been given.
summary: Mashable reports that Apple says it will soon add controls so that Full Disk Access, the Mac setting that lets an app reach files, mail, messages and browsing history, can be granted only through a very explicit user action, because AI agents raise the risks of such access. Mashable ties the move to Meta's Muse app and to Inc. columnist Jason Aten's claim that Muse synced his Messages database after he declined permission, which Meta says cannot happen if a user declines; Apple's quoted statement does not name Muse, and the plan was first reported on 2 Oct 2026 (our 3 Oct edition carried TechCrunch's report).
notes: Older news re-dated: Apple announced the plan on 2 Oct 2026 (our 3 Oct edition, item 30). Mashable calls it a response to Muse, but the Apple statement it quotes does not name Muse.
